title: Claude Skills: how to set up Claude once so you stop re-prompting
summary: Ruben explains Claude Skills as reusable instructions that live inside Claude and fire on a /command or automatically. He walks non-developers through building one with the skill-creator, then shares seven lesser-known hacks and honest limits.

principles.text: Skills package long context and instructions into the AI, so you stop re-explaining the same task.
principles.quote: It’s like a very long context + instructions, living inside the AI.

principles.text: Start your first Skill with the task you re-explain most often.
principles.quote: Don’t know which task? Pick the one you re-explain the most. That’s the one.

principles.text: Be specific when describing a Skill; vague descriptions produce Skills that don't work.
Always run the evaluation on a new Skill before installing it; most people skip the step that matters most.
principles.quote: Take the time, it’s the most important step.

principles.text: Negative triggers ("Do NOT use for...") matter more than positive ones because they stop a Skill hijacking unrelated chats.
principles.quote: The _“Do NOT use for…”_ line in your description is more important than the _“Use when…”_ line.

principles.text: Debug a broken Skill by asking Claude when it would use it, then fix the description it quotes back.
principles.quote: Ask Claude: _“When would you use the linkedin-post skill?”_
